cues.en: Let's talk a bit about tuning your neural networks.
cues.zh: 談談如何調整神經網路。

cues.en: This is not stuff that is typically taught, but I'm going to try to convey it as best as I can.
cues.zh: 這通常不是課堂會教的內容，但我會盡量傳達。

cues.en: So let's talk about learning rate.
cues.zh: 先談學習率。

cues.en: First of all what do we mean by learning rate.
cues.zh: 首先，學習率是什麼？

cues.en: Well you need to understand how these neural networks are trained.
cues.zh: 要先理解神經網路如何訓練。

cues.en: They're using a technique called gradient descent or something similar to gradient descent there's various different flavors of it out there.
cues.zh: 使用梯度下降，或類似技術，有各種不同變形。

cues.en: The basic idea is that we start at some random point of weights in our neural network and we just sample different solutions, different sets of weights, trying to minimize some cost function that we define over
cues.zh: 基本概念，是從神經網路的一組隨機權重開始，取樣不同解、不同權重組合，試著在多個

cues.en: several epochs.
cues.zh: 訓練週期中，最小化定義的成本函數。

cues.en: So those are the key words there.
cues.zh: 這些是關鍵字。

cues.en: We have many epoch, iterations, over which we train at each epoch.
cues.zh: 有很多 epoch，也就是迭代，在每個訓練週期中訓練。

cues.en: We try a different set of weights on our neural network. Trying to minimize some cost function which might be the overall accuracy of how well it makes predictions on our validation set.
cues.zh: 試不同權重組合，最小化某個成本函數，例如模型在驗證集預測的整體準確程度。

cues.en: So we need to have some sort of rhyme and reason as to how we make those samples of different solutions, different weights if you will. If we were to boil this down into sort of a two-dimensional graph maybe
cues.zh: 因此，取樣不同解、不同權重時，需要有些依據。濃縮成二維圖，可能

cues.en: it would look something like this where we're just sampling different points here along a curve of solutions and we're trying to find the one that minimizes the cost function.
cues.zh: 像這樣，沿著解的曲線取樣不同點，尋找讓成本函數最小的一個。

cues.en: So that's the the y axis here.
cues.zh: 也就是這裡的 Y 軸。

cues.en: So what we're trying to find is the lowest point on this graph and we're trying to get there by sampling it at different points and learning from each previous sample.
cues.zh: 因此，要找圖上最低點，透過在不同位置取樣，從前一次樣本學習，抵達那裡。

cues.en: That's what gradient descent is all about.
cues.zh: 這就是梯度下降。

cues.en: So the learning rate is all about how far apart those samples are.
cues.zh: 學習率，就是這些取樣點相隔多遠。

cues.en: So you see here we might have started up here and our learning rates said Okay I'm going to try another point here and we'll try again here.
cues.zh: 可以看到，也許從這裡開始，學習率說：「好，再試這裡，然後再試這裡。」

cues.en: So on and so forth until I finally find the lowest point along this curve and called out my best solution.
cues.zh: 依此類推，直到找到曲線最低點，當作最佳解。

cues.en: So not too hard to understand the effective learning rate on your training right.
cues.zh: 不難理解，學習率如何影響訓練，對吧？

cues.en: If you have too high of a learning rate you might overshoot that solution entirely.
cues.zh: 學習率太高，可能完全跨過解。

cues.en: So imagine my learning rate was huge and I went straight from here to here.
cues.zh: 想像學習率很大，直接從這裡跳到這裡。

cues.en: I might miss that bottom point there entirely if my learning rate were too high.
cues.zh: 太高，就可能完全錯過底部。

cues.en: But you can see that if my learning rate is too small I'm gonna be sampling a whole lot of different points here and it's gonna take a lot of epochs a lot of steps to actually find that optimal solution.
cues.zh: 但太小，會取樣很多點，需要很多訓練週期、很多步，才找到最佳解。

cues.en: So too high of a learning rate might mean that I overshoot the correct solution entirely but too small for learning rate will mean that my training might take longer than it needs to.
cues.zh: 因此，太高可能完全跨過正確解，太低則讓訓練時間比必要更長。

cues.en: Now learning rate is an example of what we call hyperparameters.
cues.zh: 學習率，是所謂超參數的例子。

cues.en: It's one of the knobs and dials that you use while training your deep learning model that can affect its end result.
cues.zh: 訓練深度學習模型時，可調整的旋鈕之一，能影響最終結果。

cues.en: And oftentimes these hyperparameters can have just as much influence on the quality of your model as the topology of the model.
cues.zh: 這些超參數對模型品質的影響，往往不亞於模型拓樸、

cues.en: The feature engineering you've done and everything else. So it's just another piece of the puzzle here that you need to arrive at experimentally.
cues.zh: 特徵工程，以及其他事情。所以，這是另一個必須透過實驗找出的部分。

cues.en: In addition to learning rate another important hyperparameter is the batch size and this is how many training samples are used within each epoch.
cues.zh: 除了學習率，另一個重要超參數，是批次大小，也就是每個訓練週期使用多少訓練樣本。

cues.en: Now hammer this into your heads guys because it's kind of counterintuitive. You would think that a large batch size would be a good thing.
cues.zh: 各位，一定要記住，因為有點反直覺。你會以為大批次是好事。

cues.en: Right the more data the better.
cues.zh: 對吧，資料越多越好。

cues.en: But no that's not how it ends up working.
cues.zh: 但不是，實際不是這樣。

cues.en: It turns out that if you have a small batch size it has a better ability to work its way out of what we call local minima.
cues.zh: 小批次，更有能力擺脫所謂局部最小值。

cues.en: So in this example here you can see that we have a minima here, sort of a dip in the graph here where we have a pretty good you know a nice low lost function value here.
cues.zh: 這個例子，圖上這裡有一個低谷，損失函數值已經相當低。

cues.en: What we're trying to optimize for is pretty good here but there's a risk during great descent that we get stuck in that local minima. When in fact the better solution is over here somewhere.
cues.zh: 目標在這裡已經不錯，但梯度下降可能卡在局部最小值，實際上，更好的解在另一邊。

cues.en: So we want to make sure that during the process of gradient descent we have some ability to wiggle our way out of this thing and find that better solution.
cues.zh: 因此，要確保梯度下降過程，有能力稍微擺動、離開這裡，找到更好的解。

cues.en: It turns out that smaller batch sizes can do that more effectively than larger ones.
cues.zh: 小批次，比大批次更能做到。

cues.en: So a small batch size can wiggle its way out of these local minima but a large batch size might end up getting stuck in there like basically weighing it down if you will. So batch sizes that are too large
cues.zh: 小批次能擺脫局部最小值，大批次卻可能被壓住、卡在裡面。因此，批次太大，

cues.en: can end up getting stuck in the wrong solution.
cues.zh: 可能卡在錯誤解。

cues.en: And what's even weirder is that because you will usually randomly shuffle your data at the beginning of each training epoch, this can end up manifesting itself as getting very inconsistent results from
cues.zh: 更奇怪的是，因為通常每個訓練週期開始，都會隨機打亂資料，這可能表現成每次執行，

cues.en: run to run.
cues.zh: 結果非常不一致。

cues.en: So if my batch size is just a little bit too big, maybe sometimes I'll get stuck in this minima and sometimes I won't you know and I'll see that in the end results of seeing that from run to run sometimes I'll get
cues.zh: 批次只要稍微太大，有時卡在這個最小值，有時不會，最後結果就是每次執行，有時得到

cues.en: that answer and sometimes I'll get that answer right.
cues.zh: 那個答案，有時這個答案，對吧？

cues.en: So hammer this into your head guys, smaller batch sizes tend to not get stuck in local minima but large batch sizes can converge on the wrong solution at random.
cues.zh: 所以，各位請記住，小批次通常不會卡在局部最小值，大批次卻可能隨機收斂到錯誤解。

cues.en: A large learning rate can end up overshooting the correct solution but small learning rates can increase the training time.
cues.zh: 大學習率可能跨過正確解，小學習率則可能增加訓練時間。

cues.en: So remember this.
cues.zh: 請記住。

cues.en: Write it down.
cues.zh: 寫下來。

cues.en: Important stuff and its again an example of things that most people just learned the hard way through experience.
cues.zh: 很重要，再次是多數人只能透過經驗、吃苦頭學到的事。

cues.en: But I'm trying to teach it to you up front here.
cues.zh: 但我想事先教給你。
